==== src/VerifySample.Tests/ModuleInitializer.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=MailMessage&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;

// Everything here runs once, when the test assembly loads, before any test.
public static class ModuleInitializer
{
    [ModuleInitializer]
    public static void Initialize()
    {
        // Initializes every Verify.* plugin the project references and has not initialized above.
        // Explicit calls come first so their parameters apply: a plugin can only be initialized once.
        VerifierSettings.InitializePlugins();
    }
}

==== src/VerifySample.Tests/Extensions/MailMessageTests.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=MailMessage&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using System.Net.Mail;
using System.Net.Mime;

// Verify.MailMessage: Snapshots System.Net.Mail types: a MailMessage, its attachments, alternate views and content types.
// https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.MailMessage
// Note: File converters are registered for MailMessage, Attachment, AlternateView and
// LinkedResource, so attachments are split into their own verified files.
// Note: ContentId values are generated per message, and are scrubbed to Guid_1.
// Note: No third party dependency: the mail types are part of the base class library.
public class MailMessageTests
{
    // The message is written as addresses, subject and body rather than as its object graph,
    // so the snapshot reads like the mail that would be sent.
    [Fact]
    public Task MailMessage()
    {
        var mail = new MailMessage(
            from: "from@mail.com",
            to: "to@mail.com",
            subject: "The subject",
            body: "The body");
        return Verify(mail);
    }

    // An attachment has a file converter, so its content is written as a separate verified
    // file with the extension its content type implies.
    [Fact]
    public Task Attachment()
    {
        var attachment = new Attachment(
            new MemoryStream("file content"u8.ToArray()),
            new ContentType("text/html; charset=utf-8"))
        {
            Name = "name.txt"
        };
        return Verify(attachment);
    }

    // A ContentType is verified on its own, which is useful when the code under test builds
    // one rather than a whole message.
    [Fact]
    public Task ContentType()
    {
        var content = new ContentType("text/html; charset=utf-8")
        {
            Name = "name.txt"
        };
        return Verify(content);
    }

    // The same for a ContentDisposition, which is what decides whether a client shows an
    // attachment inline or offers it as a download.
    [Fact]
    public Task ContentDisposition()
    {
        var content = new ContentDisposition("attachment; filename=\"filename.jpg\"");
        return Verify(content);
    }
}
